title: Safety audit: C hasher reused after finalize continues the old message, though b3.h says it holds none
body:
On next, `b3.h` says `b3_hasher_finalize` leaves the hasher "finished and holds no message; `b3_hasher_new` starts the next". The implementation reads the Hasher out and leaves its bytes unchanged.

Release build, exact ddb7199d7f0b0f04390e923474b630ffc7ff2811 through the C API's own entry points (`safety-capi-reuse-epyc-20261108T151551-cecf68fe`, VERIFIED): new, update("abc"), finalize, then

- finalize again: **hash("abc") again**;
- update("xyz") without new, finalize: **hash("abcxyz")**, not hash("xyz").

A cursory C reader can take "holds no message" to mean "empty and ready", and get a silently wrong digest for every message after the first. Released main 6e0dffd3 had a `const` finalize, repeatable, as official BLAKE3's C API; code ported from either keeps updating after finalize and now relies on undocumented continuation. The memory accesses stay valid (Hasher owns nothing), so this is a wrong-result and contract-clarity issue, not memory unsafety. The keyed key and staged bytes also remain in caller memory after finalize, as before.

Candidate remedies, your choice: write the fresh state for the same mode after the read (cheap: the core, not the 16 KiB stage), making the doc's sentence true; or reword b3.h to say any call other than `b3_hasher_new` on a finished hasher breaks the contract. A fail-stop check would need a state marker, which may not earn its place.

— Sam Shackleton
